b6_reason: Zero net flux through the closed surface means the inward and outward flux cancel, i.e. as many field lines enter as leave; it says nothing about E being constant or uniform, and by Gauss's law it only forces zero NET enclosed charge, not that all charges lie inside.
b6_working: Phi = closed integral of E . dS = q_enclosed/epsilon_0 = 0 => q_enclosed = 0 => inward flux = outward flux. Option 2 and 4 fail (E can vary in magnitude and direction with zero net flux, e.g. a uniform field through any closed surface, or a dipole enclosed). Option 3 fails (zero flux does not require charges to be inside; a charge outside the surface also gives zero net flux).
b6_note: Stem has two unreadable glyphs; read as the closed-surface integral of E . dS = 0 (Gauss's law flux integral), which makes the question well posed with exactly one correct option.
